Title: Right to Know / Access
Description: Consumers may request that a business disclose the categories and specific pieces of personal information it has collected about them, the categories of sources, the business/commercial purpose for collecting, and the categories of third parties with whom it is shared.

Title: Right to Data Portability
Description: Where technically feasible, a business must provide personal information disclosed under the right to know in a portable and readily usable format that allows the consumer to transmit it to another entity without hindrance.

Title: Right to Delete
Description: Consumers may request deletion of personal information a business has collected from them, subject to statutory exceptions (e.g., completing the transaction, security/fraud prevention, legal compliance, internal lawful uses compatible with the context of collection).

Title: Right to Correct (CPRA)
Description: Consumers may request correction of inaccurate personal information a business maintains about them; the business must use commercially reasonable efforts to correct it, accounting for the nature of the information and purposes of processing.

Title: Right to Know Specific Pieces and Categories Collected
Description: Consumers may request the specific pieces of personal information collected, the categories of personal information collected, and the categories of sources, purposes, and third parties, covering the 12 months preceding the request (or longer, if the business chooses).

Title: Right to Know About Sale, Sharing, and Disclosure
Description: Consumers may request the categories of personal information sold, shared, or disclosed for a business purpose, and the categories of third parties, service providers, or contractors to whom each category was sold, shared, or disclosed.

Title: Right to Opt-Out of Sale or Sharing
Description: Consumers have the right, at any time, to direct a business that sells or shares personal information to third parties not to sell or share it, including personal information sold or shared for cross-context behavioral advertising.

Title: Right to Limit Use of Sensitive Personal Information (CPRA)
Description: Consumers may direct a business to limit its use and disclosure of sensitive personal information to what is necessary to perform the services or provide the goods reasonably expected by an average consumer, or as otherwise permitted by regulation.

Title: Right to Non-Discrimination
Description: A business may not deny goods or services, charge different prices, or provide a different level or quality of goods or services because a consumer exercised a CCPA/CPRA right; financial incentives are permitted only if reasonably related to the value of the data and clearly disclosed.

Title: Notice at Collection
Description: At or before the point of collection, a business must inform consumers of the categories of personal information to be collected, the purposes for which each category will be used, whether that information is sold or shared, and the applicable retention period (or the criteria used to determine it).

Title: Privacy Policy Requirements
Description: A business must maintain a publicly available, conspicuously posted privacy policy describing its online and offline data practices, consumer rights, and the methods for submitting requests, and update it at least once every 12 months.

Title: "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Info" Link
Description: A business that sells or shares personal information must provide a clear and conspicuous link on its homepage titled "Do Not Sell or Share My Personal Information" (or a combined "Your Privacy Choices" link/icon) enabling consumers to opt out.

Title: Opt-Out Preference Signal (e.g., Global Privacy Control)
Description: A business must treat a valid opt-out preference signal received via a consumer's browser or device (such as Global Privacy Control) as a request to opt out of sale/sharing for that browser or device, and need not additionally post a separate opt-out link for that consumer's session where a signal is honored.

Title: Verification of Consumer Requests
Description: A business must establish, document, and comply with a reasonable method for verifying that the person making a request to know, delete, or correct is the consumer (or their authorized agent) about whom the business holds information, scaled to the sensitivity of the data and risk of harm from improper disclosure.

Title: Response Timelines (45-Day Statutory Clock)
Description: A business must respond to a verifiable consumer request within 45 calendar days of receipt; this period may be extended once by an additional 45 days when reasonably necessary, provided the consumer is notified of the extension and the reason within the initial 45-day period.

Title: Designated Methods for Submitting Requests
Description: A business must make available at least two designated methods for submitting requests to know, at minimum a toll-free telephone number, and (if it operates a website) an online web form or similar mechanism; requests to delete, correct, and opt-out must also be reasonably accessible.

Title: Definition: Business
Description: A for-profit legal entity that collects consumers' personal information, does business in California, determines the purposes and means of processing, and meets at least one applicability threshold: over $25M in annual gross revenue (adjusted periodically), or annually buys/sells/shares the personal information of 100,000+ consumers or households, or derives 50%+ of annual revenue from selling or sharing personal information. Applicability is based on these thresholds, not merely on being California-based.

Title: Definition: Service Provider
Description: An entity that processes personal information on behalf of a business, pursuant to a written contract, for a business purpose, and that is contractually prohibited from retaining, using, or disclosing the personal information for any purpose other than the business purposes specified in the contract or as otherwise permitted by the CCPA/CPRA.

Title: Definition: Contractor (CPRA)
Description: A CPRA-added role: an entity to which the business makes available personal information for a business purpose pursuant to a written contract, subject to use/retention/disclosure restrictions similar to a service provider, but distinguished by how it receives the data (made available by the business, rather than collected on the business's behalf).

Title: Definition: Third Party
Description: Any entity that is not the business collecting personal information, not a service provider, and not a contractor, to whom the business discloses personal information; disclosures to third parties for valuable consideration or cross-context behavioral advertising generally constitute a sale or sharing.

Title: Definition: Sale
Description: Selling, renting, releasing, disclosing, disseminating, making available, transferring, or otherwise communicating a consumer's personal information to a third party for monetary or other valuable consideration.

Title: Definition: Sharing (CPRA)
Description: A CPRA-added concept distinct from sale: disclosing or making available a consumer's personal information to a third party for cross-context behavioral advertising, whether or not for monetary or other valuable consideration -- this closed the ad-tech gap left by defining sale around consideration.

Title: Definition: Sensitive Personal Information (CPRA)
Description: A CPRA-added category including: Social Security/driver's license/state ID/passport numbers; account log-in, financial account, or payment card credentials combined with access credentials; precise geolocation; racial or ethnic origin; religious or philosophical beliefs; union membership; contents of mail, email, and text messages unless the business is the intended recipient; genetic data; biometric data used to identify a consumer; health data; and data concerning sex life or sexual orientation.

Title: Notice of Right to Limit Use of Sensitive Personal Information
Description: Where a business uses or discloses sensitive personal information for purposes beyond those necessary to provide the requested goods/services, it must provide a notice and a "Limit the Use of My Sensitive Personal Information" link enabling consumers to restrict that use.

Title: Data Minimization and Purpose Limitation (CPRA)
Description: A business's collection, use, retention, and sharing of personal information must be reasonably necessary and proportionate to achieve the purposes disclosed at collection or another compatible purpose; using personal information for a materially different purpose requires new notice and, where required, consent.

Title: Retention Limitation
Description: A business must not retain personal information for longer than is reasonably necessary to achieve the disclosed purpose(s) of collection or processing, and the applicable retention period (or the criteria for determining it) must be stated in the notice at collection and privacy policy.

Category: Service Provider / Contractor / Third Party Contracts
Title: Required Contract Terms with Service Providers and Contractors
Description: Written contracts with service providers and contractors must specify a limited and specified business purpose, prohibit selling/sharing the personal information, prohibit retaining/using/disclosing it outside the direct business relationship or contract, and require certification that the recipient understands and will comply with these restrictions.

Category: Service Provider / Contractor / Third Party Contracts
Title: Required Contract Terms with Third Parties
Description: Before selling or disclosing personal information to a third party, a business must enter into a contract that specifies the personal information is sold/disclosed only for limited, specified purposes, requires the third party to comply with the CCPA/CPRA, and grants the business rights to take reasonable steps to remediate unauthorized use.

Title: Annual Cybersecurity Audits for High-Risk Processing
Description: Businesses whose processing of personal information presents significant risk to consumers' privacy or security (per CPPA regulations, based on factors like size and sensitivity of data processed) must complete an annual, independent cybersecurity audit assessing the effectiveness of their security programs.

Title: Risk Assessments for High-Risk Processing
Description: Businesses whose processing presents significant risk to consumer privacy must conduct regular risk assessments weighing the benefits of the processing against the risks to consumers, and submit those assessments to the California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) on the schedule set by regulation.

Title: Automated Decision-Making Technology (ADMT) Access and Opt-Out
Description: CPPA rulemaking authority extends to requiring businesses to provide consumers access to, and the right to opt out of, automated decision-making technology used for significant decisions (e.g., employment, financial, or lending decisions), including profiling; implementation details are governed by CPPA regulations.

Title: Private Right of Action for Data Breaches
Description: Consumers whose nonencrypted, nonredacted personal information is breached as a result of a business's failure to implement and maintain reasonable security procedures and practices may bring a civil action for statutory damages between $100 and $750 per consumer per incident (or actual damages, if greater), without needing to show actual harm.

Title: Administrative Enforcement by the CPPA and Attorney General
Description: The California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA) and the Attorney General may investigate violations and impose administrative fines (up to $2,500 per violation, or $7,500 per intentional violation or violation involving a minor, adjusted periodically); the CPRA eliminated the general 30-day cure period that existed under the original CCPA for most violations.

Title: California Privacy Protection Agency (CPPA)
Description: The CPRA established the CPPA as the first dedicated state privacy regulator in the U.S., with authority to adopt implementing regulations, investigate violations, and enforce the CCPA/CPRA, supplementing (and in rulemaking areas, superseding) the Attorney General's role.

Title: Preemption of Conflicting Local Ordinances
Description: The CCPA/CPRA generally occupies the field with respect to the collection and sale of consumers' personal information by businesses, limiting the ability of California cities/counties to impose additional or conflicting requirements on covered businesses.

Title: Waiver Prohibition
Description: Any provision of a contract or agreement that purports to waive or limit a consumer's rights under the CCPA/CPRA is contrary to public policy, void, and unenforceable.

Title: Exemptions
Description: The CCPA/CPRA does not apply to certain categories of information already governed by other laws where specified conditions are met, including information subject to the Gramm-Leach-Bliley Act, the Fair Credit Reporting Act, the Driver's Privacy Protection Act, and certain clinical trial and HIPAA-covered health information; exemptions must be evaluated data-category by data-category, not assumed at the organization level.
